newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia live animal exports in quality bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia live animal exports in quality bid.

text.p: Australia's A$500 million livestock export industry is set to introduce a ground-breaking quality assurance system (QAS), the Australian Livestock Exporters' Council Ltd (ALEC) said on Monday.
This would cement Australia's position as world leader in livestock exports, ALEC said.
The new A$300,000 QAS would consolidate the four existing sets of standards that regulate the industry, to provide one over-arching set of regulations.

These would provide a link between on-farm schemes and on-board regulations overseen by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority, creating a chain of quality assurance from paddock to ship, ALEC said.
The QAS programme follows controversy last year when Australia's live export industry lost two ships at sea, one carrying 1,600 live cattle and the other almost 70,000 sheep.
A trial of the QAS measures was scheduled to finish in early February before a national rollout, ALEC said.

The new industry self-regulated standards would be known as LEAP, for Livestock Export Accreditation Programme. It would would encompass an industry code for incorporation into a membership code with the QAS managed by ALEC, it said.
ALEC intends that adherence to the QAS be a requirement for export and be adopted by all enterprises, it said.
LEAP will address issues from on-farm animal selection through to loading on the export vessel, it said.
Australia's live cattle exports have risen by more than 58 percent to 627,695 head in 1995/96 from 396,132 head in 1994/95.
Australia's largest customers are Indonesia, the Philippines, Egypt and Malaysia.
In 1996, Australia exported 5.8 million sheep to 18 countries, with the majority sent to Middle Eastern countries.
